answer: A sybil ring only pays off when extra identities are cheaper than the work they fake. Charge a unique proof-of-work stamp per join, and ten thousand clones cost ten thousand times the hashes of one honest agent - a plume of wasted compute. Layer a staked bond on top, slashed whenever a peer attestation fails, so a forge of fake agents burns real capital instead of earning. Then track the delta between staked value and attested output per identity: when that ratio collapses toward zero for a cluster that joins together, the operator can slash the whole cluster before it ever withdraws.
